motion: Do we need God for morality?

moves.currentDescription: Ferrer argues that conduct serving self interest or selected goals remains functional rather than categorically moral or good for its own sake.
moves.lockedProposition: Actions serving self-interest or arbitrary goals remain functional and conditional rather than categorically moral.

moves.currentDescription: Dillahunty compares wellbeing evaluation with measurement showing that chosen standards can yield non subjective judgments about consequences and conduct.
moves.lockedProposition: Subjectively selected goals can support non-subjective assessments of consequences just as an arbitrarily defined unit supports objective measurement.
